skill.name: algorithmic-art
skill.description: Creates algorithmic art concepts and p5.js browser artifacts with seeded randomness, adjustable parameters, and reusable viewer structure.

skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most high-risk static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, regular expression usage, CSS, and p5.js template comments. The only confirmed issues are low-severity external network dependencies for p5.js and Google Fonts in generated browser artifacts.

remediation.issue: Generated artifacts load p5.js from a third-party CDN.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle p5.js locally or document the CDN dependency clearly. Keep subresource integrity on any external script reference.

remediation.issue: Generated artifacts load Google Fonts from external domains.
remediation.suggestion: Use local font fallbacks or self-host fonts when offline use or privacy-sensitive use is required.

remediation.issue: The SKILL.md HTML example references p5.js without an integrity attribute.
remediation.suggestion: Mirror the viewer template by adding integrity and crossorigin attributes to the documentation example.

content.value_statement: Generative art prompts often produce static visuals without a clear computational idea. This skill turns a concept into a philosophy, then into a seeded p5.js viewer with controls.
actual_capabilities: Creates a written algorithmic philosophy for a generative art movement.
Guides p5.js implementation with seeded randomness for reproducible outputs.
Uses a browser viewer template with sidebar controls and seed navigation.
Supports adjustable parameters such as counts, scales, speeds, thresholds, and colors.
Produces a single HTML artifact intended to run in a browser or Claude artifact view.
Includes a JavaScript template with common generative art structure and utilities.
limitations: Generated HTML may rely on external CDN and font services unless modified.
The skill gives creative guidance but does not guarantee visual quality.
It focuses on p5.js browser art, not native apps or rendered video pipelines.
Large particle systems may need performance tuning for slower devices.

use_cases.title: Prototype Interactive Art
use_cases.description: Turn a concept into a p5.js artwork with adjustable parameters and reproducible seeds.

use_cases.title: Teach Generative Systems
use_cases.description: Show how philosophy, randomness, noise, particles, and parameters connect in creative coding.

use_cases.title: Explore Visual Directions
use_cases.description: Generate refined computational art directions before committing to a final visual system.

prompt_templates.title: Start From A Theme
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an algorithmic art philosophy from this theme: [theme]. Then outline the p5.js behaviors and parameters it needs.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Viewer Artifact
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the algorithmic-art skill to create one self-contained p5.js HTML artifact for [concept]. Include seed controls and parameter sliders.

prompt_templates.title: Tune An Existing Sketch
prompt_templates.prompt: Refine this p5.js generative art idea for stronger composition, reproducible seeds, balanced colors, and smoother performance: [idea].

prompt_templates.title: Create A Variation System
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a seed-driven variation system for [subject]. Define the philosophy, parameter model, interaction controls, and gallery-quality p5.js implementation.

output_examples.input: A visual system inspired by ocean currents and archival maps.
output_examples.output: A philosophy named Tidal Cartography, plus a p5.js viewer with flow fields, seed controls, contour density, current speed, and muted map colors.

output_examples.input: An interactive artwork about crystal growth under pressure.
output_examples.output: A stochastic crystallization concept with particle relaxation, reproducible seeds, growth tension controls, palette options, and a downloadable canvas.

output_examples.input: A design team needs a computational background for a product launch.
output_examples.output: A polished generative direction with a concise manifesto, controlled variation, brand-aware colors, and browser-ready interaction controls.

best_practices: Start with a clear conceptual seed before writing the p5.js algorithm.
Keep randomness seeded so every important output can be reproduced.
Expose only meaningful parameters that change the artwork in understandable ways.
anti_patterns: Do not create static images when the request needs generative behavior.
Do not add many random controls without a clear artistic purpose.
Do not remove seed navigation from the viewer template.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates an algorithmic philosophy and a p5.js HTML viewer for interactive generative art.

faq.question: Can outputs be reproduced?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill emphasizes seeded randomness so the same seed can recreate the same result.

faq.question: Does it create finished images?
faq.answer: It focuses on interactive browser artifacts. Users can export canvas images from the viewer when supported.

faq.question: Does it require a build system?
faq.answer: No. The intended output is a single HTML file with inline code and controls.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Are there network dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes. The template uses external p5.js and Google Fonts URLs unless the generated artifact is modified.
